title: Cluster 01 DRILL: Innate Immunity and Infection
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 9, Extension Topic A · 9 questions · 67 marks · 30 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour · every question is an actual exam paper question
los_html:
Learning outcomes, against the questions that test them.
(a) the non-specific (innate) immune system: first line, physical, chemical and biological barriersQ1(a), Q1(b), Q1(c), Q1(d), Q3(a)
(a) innate second line: phagocytes and phagocytosisQ2(a), Q2(b), Q2(c), Q2(d), Q2(e), Q4(a)
(a) innate second line: natural killer cells, and what they killQ3(a), Q3(b)
(a) innate defensive proteins: cytokines, interferon, complementQ3(c), Q3(d), Q5(a), Q5(b), Q9(a)
(a) inflammation, its two vascular changes and its four signs; feverQ4(b), Q4(c), Q8(b), Q9(b), Q9(c)
(a) antigen, antigen presentation and the antigen-presenting cellQ7(a), Q7(b), Q7(c), Q7(d)
(a) innate against adaptive, and each system enhancing the otherQ3(d), Q6(a), Q6(b), Q8(a)
(b) roles of B and T lymphocytes, APCs and memory cellsCluster 2
(c) antibody structure related to function, IgGQ6(b) at opsonisation level only; Cluster 2 owns it
(d) somatic recombination, hyper-mutation and class switchingCluster 2
(e) vaccination controlling disease, herd immunity, smallpoxCluster 3
(f) benefits and risks of vaccinationCluster 3
(g) viruses causing disease through disruption of host tissue and functionsQ4(c), Q4(d) at stimulus level only; Cluster 3 owns it
(h) modes of transmission and infection of bacterial pathogensCluster 3
(i) modes of action of antibiotics, including penicillinCluster 3
(j) the basic reproduction number, R0Cluster 3
(k) outbreak, epidemic and pandemicCluster 3
reach-back Book 1: lysosome structure, membrane fluidity, saturated against unsaturated tailsQ2(c), Q2(e)
reach-back Book 2: transcription factors, gene expression as an outputQ3(b), Q8(b)
reach-back Book 3: ligand, receptor, transduction, cascade; immune surveillance of tumoursQ3(b), Q8(b), Q9(a)
reach-back Book 4: peptidoglycan, NAG and NAM, the gram-negative outer membraneQ1(c)

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers and not only duplicated labels. Q1 the first line at a mucosal surface, and two pathogens that defeat it · Q2 phagocytosis by compartment, organelle and membrane · Q3 the innate cells and proteins that act on host cells rather than on microbes · Q4 the whole innate cycle from breach to symptom · Q5 complement, and innate proteins in an unfamiliar fluid · Q6 the two systems compared, and what antibody hands back to the innate system · Q7 antigen, presentation and the bridge into the third line · Q8 innate immunity read off a signal transduction pathway · Q9 cell signalling as the mechanism of coordination.

The one shared marking point in the set is that phagocytosis occurs, which Q2 needs alongside the compartment names and Q4(a) needs alongside PRR recognition and phagocyte recruitment. The two schemes credit different halves of the outcome, so the answers do not collapse into each other; if you gave Q2's phagosome answer in Q4(a) you answered the wrong half. Nothing else in the set repeats.

Nothing from Clusters 2 or 3, and nothing from Book 4's viral cycles. Clonal selection, clonal expansion, primary against secondary responses, MHC class I against class II in full, antibody diversity, the four types of immunity, vaccination, R0 and the epidemiology terms are all later. No question here sets a viral replication cycle, which belongs to Core Idea 2 LO 2(e) in Book 4.
